function.name: give_up
function.arguments: {"reason": "Five closing attempts at wrist-camera-verified positions (x=-0.086 to -0.156, y=0.059-0.070, z=0.86) all ended with the gripper reading 0.016 (closed on air, no contact), so the block was never grasped. With only two calls left after this one, lift, carry to the bowl, release, and done cannot all fit, so I am stopping rather than leaving the task half-done.", "hindsight": "The move_to tool runs the full interpolation (~80 steps) only when the gripper dimension changes; cartesian-only calls advance only 2-3 servo steps (~1cm), so budget moves around gripper state changes. The wrist camera is tilted with an off-axis mount: the block can appear centered while the jaw pads pass beside it, and the block disappears from the wrist view when it is under the palm. Use the measured gripper value after closing (about 0.016 means air, an intermediate 0.3-0.5 means holding) as the grasp verdict instead of re-reading images. Grep-style sweeps at a fixed z across a line of x targets with a close at each would locate the block faster than image servoing."}
